plugboard: AX BZ CY DG ET IP JN OQ RV SW
indicator_notes: Published M4 Shark (Triton) signal of 6 March 1945, header 'SHARK SIGNAL 6 MAR 45: 1414/6/36 90'. The published machine settings (cryptocellar.org, Jason Parker-Burlingham's break, 25 Oct 2026) are: M4, thin reflector B, Greek wheel gamma, rotors IV V III, rings A A P U, start Z K S A, plugs AX BZ CY DG ET IP JN OQ RV SW. 'start' ZKSA is the message-body starting position as stated by the source (greek Z, then K S A). Encrypted indicator: the first two groups CXSO UNVZ (8 letters). The final two groups of the published 90-group block, also CXSO UNVZ, are a repeat and are excluded from the body. The source does not give a separate Grundstellung. Body position check: decrypting ciphertext letters 9-352 with ZKSA reproduces the published plaintext exactly (verified independently with a software M4 simulation).
notes: Plaintext is the raw decryption 'with no corrections applied or encoding undone' as published (344 letters, 86 groups). The source also gives a corrected, word-divided version (14 letters changed, not itemised) which is not used here. The message uses 4-letter groups. The page's own claim that the solver used an AI model is not relied upon for this record.

plugboard: CY EL FH GS IJ KQ MW PV RZ TU
indicator_notes: Heeresgruppe Nord key table for 8 July 1941 (Schluesseltafel): 'B432 pkf', plugs CY EL FH GS IJ KQ MW PV RZ TU. Message Nr. 23, Kenngruppe KHLPT, indicator OKF QLV, Start PIK, Stop PMA (the PIK/PMA pair is printed on the line above the Nr. 23 row in the PDF layout). The source lists Start PIK, which is taken as the message-body start position. The source does not state how the indicator decodes, and the Grundstellung is not given separately. Rotor order is read left-to-right as IV III II (source 'B432'). A check decryption of the 120-letter body with these settings gives German text beginning INFX RG T X EINS X DREI X, which supports the reading, but that check is not a published plaintext.
notes: Kenngruppe KHLPT stripped; the ciphertext is the 120-letter body reported as '125 / 120' in the key table. No published plaintext for Nr. 23 was found in the sources read, so 'plaintext' is empty. The task's 'Barbarossa operation' two-part message was not located with settings and plaintext. Rotor order and start-position readings are inferred from the table layout (see indicator_notes) and were only checked by plausibility of decryption, so treat 'rotors' and 'start' as the less certain fields.
